newsitem.title: USA: JC Penney strong, most U.S. retailer sales at plan.
newsitem.headline: JC Penney strong, most U.S. retailer sales at plan.

text.p: Most U.S. retailer sales for February came in at or slightly above expectations, with J.C. Penney Co Inc among the leaders with an 11.4 percent same-store sales gain, slightly above some analysts expectations.
Wal-Mart Stores Inc, with a 6.7 percent gain in same-store sales, or sales at stores open at least a year, was also slightly higher than expected.
"Wal-Mart was somewhat of a surprise to me," said Mike Niemira, analsyt at Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi. "They had talked about weaker numbers kind of before."
Other upside suprises were two electronics superstores, Best Buy Co Inc and Circuit City Stores Inc's Circuit City Group, which were both less weak than expected.

Best Buy reported a decline of three percent in same-store sales, while the Circuit City Group posted a four percent decline. Some analysts had forecast a declines of 7-10 percent for the electronics superstores, which have been trailing other retailers in recent months.
On the other end, Sears, Roebuck and Co came in with a 1.6 percent gain, below the 2-4 percent gain analysts had been forecasting. Gap posted flat same-store sales.

Sears shares were down 5/8 at 55 Thursday, with Gap down 1-1/4 at 32-1/2. JC Penney was up 7/8 at 50, Best Buy was up one at 9-5/8, Circuit City rose 2-1/8 to 33-7/8, Wal-Mart was unchanged at 26-5/8, and Saks Holdings Inc, which posted a 6.4 percent same-store sales gain, was up 3/4 at 34-3/4.
